newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling eases in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling eases in quiet trading.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling opened Tuesday's trading a touch weaker in a very quiet market after a long weekend, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted the shilling at a mean average of 54.89 against the dollar from 54.88 on Friday. Against the pound, it was posted at an average of 90 from 89.89.
Dealers said they were trading within very tight ranges with the shilling stuck at 54.85/95 levels.
"Apart from a few dollars from the agriculturals, the market is very quiet," a dealer said.
"The market is quiet, with very little interbank activity going on. We've seen very little interest from both sides this morning," another dealer added.
They however said they expected activity to pick up this week on inflows from coffee, tea and horticultural sales.
The money market market remained liquid with overnight rates quoted below ten percent for the third consecutive week.
